title: Signal Conductor: unified eval regression orchestration and alert routing for Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When model or config changes land, the eval system currently emits many semi-duplicate regression notices across datasets, prompt slices, and metric thresholds. Users see noisy Slack threads and duplicated PagerDuty pages during rollouts. This leads to missed signal, higher operational load, and frustrated product owners.

Scope: Build a Console-hosted orchestration layer ("Signal Conductor") that: groups related eval regressions originating from the same change window; surfaces a single root alert with provenance and contributing sub-signals; supports deduplication thresholds and sticky suppression; routes delivered notices to Slack channels and PagerDuty services with configurable dedupe and notification policies; integrates with rollouts/canary metadata so users can link a regression to a model/config deploy; and exposes UI controls for escalating, muting, and attaching runbooks.

Non-goals: This ticket does not replace low-level eval computation or thresholding logic (handled by Evals pipeline) and does not implement full-featured root-cause automation in the first iteration.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Console shows a consolidated "signal view" where regressions that share the same change window and at least one overlapping cohort are grouped into a single 'incident' with provenance links to the underlying eval runs.
2) Slack integration: grouped incidents send a single threaded notification with a summary card, top 3 contributing metrics, and a link to the Console incident. Duplicate notifications suppressed for 24h by default.
3) PagerDuty integration: a single PagerDuty incident is opened for the grouped signal when severity=high and routes to the configured escalation policy; subsequent related signals attach to the same incident instead of opening new pages.
4) Deduplication rules are configurable: by metric family, by model version, by config diff id, and by custom tag. Admins can set suppression windows and sticky suppression.
5) Console UI exposes an action menu on the incident: acknowledge, mute (with duration), escalate, attach runbook, and mark false-positive.
6) E2E tests and an integration smoke test with a staged model rollout are present in the evals-ci pipeline.
tasks: Design incident grouping heuristic (change-window + cohort overlap + top-n metrics)
Backend: implement signal aggregator service and incident model in console-api
Backend: dedupe policy engine with configurable rules stored in workspace settings
Integrations: Slack message formatting + thread attachment, suppression mechanism
Integrations: PagerDuty single-incident attach behavior and severity mapping
UI: incident list view, incident detail page with provenance panel and actions
Telemetry: emit grouping metrics and dedupe false-positive rate for 30d
Testing: add regression scenario harness to evals-ci and canary runbook
updates: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial scoping meeting with Eng and Design. Agreed on grouping heuristic using a 'change window' anchored to deploy time plus overlapping cohort threshold of >=20% sample overlap.

2026-02-28 - Marco Ruiz: Proposed API shape documented in Confluence: /api/v1/console/incidents and /api/v1/console/incidents/{id}/signals. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/Signal+Conductor+Spec

2026-03-03 - Eng lead (Sofia Kim): Chose Redis streams for short-lived aggregation buffer; long-term store in postgres.incidents table. Raised concern about write amplification; ENG-21844 opened to prototype batching approach.
2026-03-05 - Design (Liam O'Connor): Posted mockups for incident cards and Slack summary block. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/signal-conductor

2026-03-08 - Marco Ruiz: Integrated a first-pass Slack message with thread stub to dev workspace (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CDEV12345/p167...), observed duplicate notifications when parallel eval jobs finish; suppression logic iteration required.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: PM review - updated acceptance criteria to require attach-to-existing-PagerDuty-incident when severity=high. Set due_date to 2026-04-02 and requested an estimate bump if ENG-21844 grows.
risks: Grouping heuristic may merge unrelated regressions if cohorts are broad — could hide real P1 incidents
PagerDuty semantics across customers vary; mis-mapping severity could cause over/under-notification
Performance: real-time signal aggregation may add latency during heavy rollout windows
Operational: suppression windows tuned too aggressively could mask regressions for subteams
qa_notes: Simulate multi-dataset regen with the regression-harness and verify a single Console incident is created
Validate Slack thread suppression by launching three related eval runs within the 30m window
Verify PagerDuty incident is attached rather than duplicated for severity=high scenario
